claims: "Integrity" is the name given to the NASA Orion spacecraft used for the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission launched four astronauts around the Moon in April 2026.
The name "Integrity" was selected by the crew to represent trust, respect, and unity.
The capsule successfully completed a 10-day mission.
The capsule splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
The Integrity Capsule (Artemis II) is the first crewed spacecraft to go beyond low Earth orbit since the Apollo era.
The crew of Artemis II consisted of Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The capsule features an AVCOAT heat shield.
The AVCOAT heat shield is designed to withstand high-speed re-entry around Mach 33.
The name "Integrity" symbolizes the "integrated effort" of NASA and the Canadian Space Agency to return humans to the Moon.
Following splashdown, the capsule is recovered and returned to Johnson Space Center for study.
In some mission communication contexts, "Integrity" is also used as the call sign for Mission Control.
